description.value: The study examined whether fMRI activation elicited by viewing high-calorie food pictures predicts weight loss during a 12-week psychosocial weight-loss program and weight maintenance during a subsequent 9-month follow-up, and whether activation changes from pre- to post-treatment.

design.value: Longitudinal fMRI study of obese and overweight adults scanned before and after a 12-week psychosocial weight-loss treatment, with a 9-month follow-up weight measurement; normal-weight controls were scanned twice 12 weeks apart.

description.value: Measure of hunger completed before the scans on a 0–150 VAS rating scale.
Participants sorted 60 laminated color pictures of foods and cars into pictures seen in the magnet and pictures not seen.
A proxy measure of adiposity using height and weight.

source_definition.value: Body mass index at the initial scan, included as a covariate in all analyses.
Percent weight change during the 12-wk program.
Weight change from the end of the program until the final weight measurement, over the 9-mo post-treatment period.

description.value: 25 obese (n = 21) and overweight (n = 4) adults enrolled in the 12-wk EatRight Lifestyle Weight Management Program; for brevity the authors refer to this group as obese.

inclusion_criteria.value: Participants were enrolled in the 12-wk EatRight Lifestyle Weight Management Program.

exclusion_criteria.value: Participants were excluded if they were left-handed and/or had an intelligence quotient < 80 on the Shipley Institute of Living Scale.

Participants were also excluded for having a chronic health or neurological condition, history of head injury or loss of consciousness for more than 5 min, history of psychosis, current or past alcohol or drug abuse problem, or being a cigarette smoker.
Participants were excluded for having ferromagnetic material in the body, being claustrophobic, or being pregnant.
Participants were excluded for having worse than 20/40 vision not correctable with contact lenses or the non-ferromagnetic corrective glasses used at the magnet.

Participants were excluded for having blood pressure > 140/90 not controlled by medication, meeting the full criteria for any eating disorder, being concurrently enrolled in another weight-loss program, and/or any food preferences or allergies inconsistent with our food pictures.
Obese participants were also excluded for body weight of > 350 lb (159 kg) and/or girth > 64 in (163 cm).

recruitment_method.value: Obese participants were recruited at one of the first three (of 12) EatRight classes. Normal-weight control participants were recruited from UAB and the surrounding community using flyers and advertisements posted in the UAB Reporter newspaper.

medical_condition.value: Two obese participants were on medication (metformin, glipizide, and/or lantus) to manage Type II diabetes.

clinical_characteristics.value: Initial BMI range was 28.4 to 44.6 kg/m2 (mean ± SD: 32.86 ± 3.82).

medication_status.value: Two obese participants were on medication to manage Type II diabetes; three obese participants were being treated with antidepressants and had been on medication for more than 6 months without changing medication between the first and second scanning sessions.

excluded_count.value: Two control participants, both men, had to be excluded because they did not return for the second scanning session.

inclusion_criteria.value: Normal-weight controls were defined as having BMI < 25.

recruitment_method.value: Recruited from UAB and the surrounding community using flyers and advertisements posted in the UAB Reporter newspaper.

task_name.value: viewing high-calorie food vs. control pictures

task_description.value: Visual stimuli were presented in a block design format during six 3:15 min runs. Each run consisted of two pseudorandomly presented epochs each of car and low-calorie food images, and one epoch each of high-calorie sweet food and high-calorie savory food images. Each epoch lasted 21 s and included 7 images presented for 2.5 s followed by a 0.5 s gap; epochs were separated by 9 s of blank screen with a fixation cross.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to eat a normal breakfast and then refrain from eating for 8 h before being imaged; to abstain from alcohol for 24 h, avoid exercise on the day of the study, and avoid caffeine for 3 h prior to imaging.

stimuli.value: 504 high-quality color photographs, including 168 food images and 84 control images for each scanning session. The food images included 84 high-calorie foods and 84 low-calorie foods; high-calorie images consisted of equal numbers of sweet and savory foods. Control images were pictures of cars.

task_performance_measures.value: Percentage of pictures correctly identified as having been seen during each fMRI scan.

instrument.value: Philips Achieva 3 T ultra-short (1.57 m) bore magnet

description.value: High resolution T1-weighted scans were acquired using a 160-slice 3D T1 Turbo-field Echo (TFE) volume sequence with T1 = 400 ms, TR = 9.9 ms, TE = 4.6 ms, flip angle = 8°, FOV = 24 cm, 256 × 256 matrix size, and 1 mm slice thickness. These were used to exclude participants with gross brain abnormality.

instrument.value: Philips Achieva 3 T ultra-short (1.57 m) bore magnet; 6-channel or 8-channel head coil

description.value: Functional MR images were acquired using single-shot gradient echo T2*-weighted echo-planar imaging (EPI) with blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) contrast. Six 3:15 min runs were acquired in each scanning session. Each volume comprised 30, 4 mm axial slices with a 1 mm interslice gap.

pulse_sequence_type.value: single-shot gradient echo T2*-weighted echo-planar imaging (EPI)

description.value: Functional images were slice time-corrected, spatially realigned, spatially normalized to standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) brain space, spatially smoothed, high-pass filtered, and temporally filtered using an autoregressive model.

steps.value: Slice time-corrected to the onset of the 15th slice (middle slice).
Spatially realigned using INRIAlign, a motion correction algorithm unbiased by local signal changes.
A mean functional image was computed for each run and matched to the EPI template provided within SPM8.
Spatially normalized to standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) brain space.
Spatially smoothed using a three-dimensional Gaussian kernel of 6 mm full-width at half-maximum (FWHM), resulting in a resampled in-plane resolution of 2 × 2 × 2 mm voxels.
Passed through a 1/128 Hz high-pass filter in order to remove low-frequency artifacts.
Temporally filtered using an autoregressive (AR(1)) model.

model_settings.value: Separate regressors were created for high-calorie food, low-calorie food, and car images by convolving the time course of activation, using a boxcar function, with the canonical HRF. Fixed-effects analyses were performed for each individual participant for both imaging sessions.

Second level (group) analyses were performed using a random-effects model of the beta images from the single-subject contrast maps. Multiple regressions related activation for the high-calorie foods vs. cars contrast to percent weight change using data from the obese group only.

description.value: High-calorie sweet foods, such as a slice of chocolate cake or cheesecake.
High-calorie savory foods, such as a cheeseburger or french fries.
Low-fat foods, such as broiled fish or salad.
Pictures of cars; these images were moderately engaging control stimuli that matched the low-calorie food images in ratings of pleasantness.

name.value: Session 1: high-calorie food images vs. control images in obese participants, reward ROI analysis

roi_definition.value: structurally defined using templates from the WFU Pickatlas toolbox within SPM8 using the AAL or Talairach Daemon atlases; nucleus accumbens and VTA/SN used predefined spheres and composite ROI

roi_label.value: anterior cingulate cortex, amygdala, caudate/putamen, hippocampus, insula, medial prefrontal cortex, nucleus accumbens, and ventral tegmental area/substantia nigra

definition.value: activation in response to high-calorie foods vs. control images

coordinate_space.value: standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) brain space

inference_level.value: cluster-level inference for contiguous voxels and voxel-level inference

multiple_comparison_method.value: false discovery rate (FDR) and family-wise error (FWE) correction

interpretations.value: greater activation to high-calorie food images than control images in reward-associated regions
